@dior is showing its first signs of a rebound under @jonathan.anderson!

LVMH announced that its Fashion and Leather Goods division grew 1% organically in the second quarter of 2026, marking its first quarterly growth since Q2 2024. While Dior’s individual figures were not disclosed, the house reportedly returned to positive territory and performed slightly above the division average.

LVMH credited the recovery to the success of Jonathan Anderson’s first designs for Dior, including strong demand for womenswear, bags and his reinterpretations of house icons such as the Lady Dior, alongside the performance of Louis Vuitton’s new stores in Beijing and Seoul, strong sales at Tiffany and Bulgari, Sephora’s growth, and a recovery in champagne and cognac.

Ever since Jonathan Anderson took over at Dior, all eyes have been on what fashion’s busiest designer would do next. Now, the results are starting to show in the numbers.

Swipe to hear what LVMH’s leadership had to say about Dior’s return to growth.

Words by Josephine Jiang

Next-Level Fashion, Daily.
Follow @a2z_fashionmag Now.

📷Vogue Runway

#dior #jonathananderson #lvmh

posts.caption:
Girls Just Wanna Have Fun in @alarakocman’s graduate collection. Presented at the University of Applied Arts Vienna (@modeklasse), the collection looks back at girlhood and the familiar rituals of dressing up, playing with exaggerated proportions to capture that space between childhood and growing up.
The oversized pumps created with @888lenn recreate the childhood memory of slipping into your mum’s heels. Far too big, slightly awkward, but all part of the fun. Their elongated proportions create the illusion of wearing shoes several sizes too large, while a hidden inner construction keeps the foot securely in place.
Another standout is the double bag: a tiny handbag for the essentials paired with an oversized shopper for everything else. It turns that familiar experience of going out with one bag and somehow ending up with far more to carry into a playful fashion object.
Swipe to see the collection!
Words by Josephine Jiang

A Dilara bride was never going to follow the rules.
@dilarafindikoglu introduces an eight-piece bridal capsule, transforming her signature corsetry, lingerie-inspired layers, frayed ruffles and shredded lace through a palette of aged ivory, champagne, baby pink and grey-blue.
Raised in a traditional household, Dilara Findikoglu has long been sceptical of conventional ideas of marriage. Yet she describes herself as a “hopeless romantic” who believes in eternal love. The collection embodies this tension, unconventional and rebellious, yet still carrying the softness and fantasy of a romantic dream.
“I don’t think a bride has to stop feeling sensual just because she’s getting married. Romance and sensuality can exist together.”

Charli XCX’s Music, Fashion, Film has arrived!

If Brat was a cultural reset, Music, Fashion, Film feels like an expansion of Charli’s creative universe, one where music, cinema, and image exist on equal footing.

The album artwork unites three figures from entirely different creative worlds: musician John Cale, fashion designer Marc Jacobs, and filmmaker Martin Scorsese - a fitting visual manifesto for a record that dissolves the boundaries between disciplines.

Produced by longtime collaborators A.G. Cook and Finn Keane, the album marks Charli’s next chapter following Brat, while continuing her fascination with image-making as much as music-making. Fashion has always existed at the center of Charli’s world - not as aesthetic, but as authorship. Music, Fashion, Film continues that language, treating clothing, cultural references, and visual identity as inseparable from the music itself.

The album is out now.

#CharliXCX #MusicFashionFilm #ArchivedRunway

Gentle Monster has unveiled the second design from its upcoming intelligent eyewear collection, developed in partnership with Google and Samsung. Marking the brand’s first venture into wearable technology, the collection merges Gentle Monster’s signature optical language with everyday intelligent functionality.
The newly revealed design features a clean square optical frame, offering a more understated expression of the collection while extending the brand’s design vocabulary into a familiar everyday silhouette. Starring Alex Consani and Anok Yai, the campaign offers the first glimpse of Gentle Monster’s fashion-forward vision for intelligent eyewear.
Compatible with both Android and iOS devices, the eyewear supports music playback, voice calls, photography, real-time translation, navigation, and hands-free interaction through Google Gemini. Designed for everyday wear, the frames offer up to nine hours of battery life on a single charge, with the charging case providing seven or more additional full charges.
The full collection will be unveiled later this fall.

posts.alt_text:
“[The Buccaneers] is not your traditional period drama – it’s funny, romantic and wildly different from anything I’ve done before,” says @alishaboe. The Norwegian-American actor’s career has spanned everything from Paranormal Activity 4 and Karen Maine’s coming-of-ager Yes, God, Yes to Jesse Eisenberg’s directorial debut, When You Finish Saving the World, though she remains best known for playing Jessica Davis in Netflix’s 13 Reasons Why.⁠
⁠
Born in Oslo, Boe began acting at an after-school drama club when she was five. After moving to Los Angeles, she became increasingly involved in her high school’s theatre programme, setting her on a path towards the screen. Now, Boe is the face of @yslbeauty’s famously nostalgic Black Opium fragrance. Its latest iteration, Pink Glaze, offers a fruitier take on the dense, sweet and peppery classic. “It’s bold, it’s magnetic, it just has this playfulness,” she says.⁠
⁠
At the link in bio, @rose_dodd speaks with Boe about her childhood acting ambitions, her latest projects and her first encounters with the ultimate “party girl” perfume 📲⁠
⁠
📸 Alisha Boe for YSL Black Opium Pink Glaze. Courtesy of @yslbeauty⁠

“Who wants to scroll, choosing men like a catalogue?” says @alejandrogomezpalomo, creative director of @palomospain. “I’m much more interested in the magic of physicality.” It is an idea that runs through the Spanish designer’s work, which recasts queer desire through theatricality, romance and the pleasure of being seen.
This approach underpins Palomo Spain’s collaboration with @tomoffinlandfoundation, marked during @prideamsterdam with a commemorative lunch. Created by the Finnish artist Touko Laaksonen, Tom of Finland’s illustrations remain one of queer culture’s defining visual languages.
Palomo’s reading of Laaksonen’s work also inspired an accompanying editorial, photographed by Kees de Klein and Cain Isan Wittenhaus. Rather than dwelling on the darker mythology associated with cruising, the black-and-white images suggest tenderness and recall James Bidgood’s dreamlike romanticism.
@pedromvasconcelos speaks with Palomo at the link in bio 📲

“I love to capture a moment in order to never forget that feeling,” says @adam_peter. In his first photography book, No Birds, the Paris-based French photographer and director turns his camera towards the forgotten stretches of inertia, examining the subtleties of friendship across rural, suburban Australia.⁠
⁠
More personal and open-ended than his commercial work, the project depended on his familiarity with model @ap.olline. “I rarely shoot someone I don’t know,” he says. “We wanted to explore expressions and emotions she hadn’t shown on camera before.” Like Sophie Calle and Gregory Shephard’s No Sex Last Night, in which a deteriorating relationship is documented during a road trip, No Birds uses a cross-country odyssey to examine the intimacy between photographer and subject – an intimacy that is exposed and intensified by being removed from familiar surroundings. ⁠
⁠
@billymparker speaks with @adam_peter at the link in bio 📲⁠
⁠
📸 No Birds by Adam Peter Johnson

posts.caption:
Beginning with his Great Patriotic War-set Ivan’s Childhood, auteur Andrei Tarkovsky made just seven features over the span of 24 years. But despite the restrictive creative conditions of the Soviet Union’s Brezhnev era, all of his films feel completely uncompromised. ⁠
⁠
Tarkovsky earned the reputation of a ‘slow cinema’ master, using long takes and experimenting with rhythm and duration as a film’s driving force.  He frequently collaborated with co-writers, including the prolific director Andrei Konchalovsky, digging deeper into his recurring themes of creation, the soul and the divine, lost innocence, a decaying world and the subconscious (the director often documented his dreams in a detailed journal). His influence is clear on filmmakers as wide-ranging as Terrence Malick, Lars von Trier and Alex Garland.⁠
⁠
Tarkovsky made his first five films in the Soviet Union before turning to Europe for his final two features, Nostalghia in Italy and The Sacrifice in Sweden – both films have just received a 4K restoration and are being re-released by @curzoncinemas this month. ⁠
⁠
To mark the double re-release of the director’s final films, @rurydoherty revisits five films that define Tarkovsky’s poetic and spectral cinema 📲⁠
⁠
📸 Film stills⁠
⁠
#AndreiTarkovsky

Harper’s Bazaar India digital cover star, Maye Musk (@mayemusk), started modelling as a teenager. She stopped at 22 to get married and raise three children, then picked it back up at 28—an age the industry considered, at the time, well past the point of no return. So she built her nutrition practice in parallel. By 31, she was in high demand as a model and continued part-time; in her 60s, she was doing high fashion. “If someone had told me as a teenager that I would be in Delhi for a top fashion magazine at 78, I would have thought they were crazy,” she says. “Yet, here I am, working alongside a very creative team.

posts.caption:
On Amami Island, craftsmen still practise dorozome in the subtropical heat, using the traditional mud-dyeing techniques of their ancestors to give local silk its distinctive earthy tones. A thousand miles to the north, artisans continue to blanket Niigata’s fields with crepe fabric in winter, allowing the snow to gently bleach their delicate Ojiya-chijimi cloth.
The legacy of such textile traditions endures not only in small workshops scattered across Japan but also in the modern mills that supply some of the world’s largest fashion brands, from Levi’s to Chanel.
Elizabeth Beattie explores why Japan remains fashion’s quiet textile powerhouse. Read more #linkinbio

Today, just about every major fashion and beauty company has a sports strategy. At the recent World Cup, companies ranging from Unilever to Levi’s were promoting products or launching activations.

posts.caption:
Who are the most desirable companies to work for in fashion? Between April and May 2026, 1173 current, aspiring and previous fashion workers shared their top three most desirable fashion employers.
For each of the top 10 companies, BoF breaks down the findings into three parts:
• The Macro Driver: the main reason respondents are attracted to the company.
• The Talent Pull: why current fashion workers say they would jump ship and join the company.
• Insiders’ Perspectives: a qualitative read drawn from recent reviews by current and former full-time employees published on Glassdoor and Indeed between December 2024 and May 2026, where available.
To weigh desirability against reality, the ranking gives the greatest weight to the people best placed to judge: those already working in the industry. “Insiders are the ones who have a better sense of whether it is truly a good place to work beyond what they see from the outside,” said  @sheena.butler.young, BoF’s senior correspondent for workplace and talent.
To read the full findings from the survey, download the full BoF Careers report: How AI Is Reshaping the Battle for Fashion and Beauty Talent. #linkinbio

posts.caption:
Artist Betye Saar, whose work reflected Black identity, culture and spirituality, died Sunday morning in Los Angeles at 99.
Saar's death was confirmed Monday by relatives. She would have turned 100 this week.
"Her symbolically rich body of work has evolved over time to demonstrate the environmental, cultural, political, racial, technological, economic, and historical context in which it exists," according to Roberts Projects, the Los Angeles gallery that represents her.
Made in 1969, her work "Black Girl's Window" was considered groundbreaking, but wasn't widely celebrated until decades later, along with it being acquired by the Museum of Modern Art in New York in 2019. "The Liberation of Aunt Jemima," created in 1972, is another one of her most important — and complex — works.
Read more about Saar's life and work at the link in @cnn's bio.
📷: Xavier Collin/Image Press Agency/Sipa USA/AP; David Sprague/Artist and Roberts Projects, Los Angeles/AP; Joshua Lott/AFP/Getty Images
posts.alt_text:
A record-high 73% of US adults say that President Donald Trump hasn't paid enough attention to the country's most important problems, a new CNN poll conducted by SSRS finds, with just 27% saying he's had the right priorities.

That comes amid increasingly bleak views of the Iran war, stagnating economic unhappiness, and broad discontent about Trump's approach to these challenges.

Roughly two-thirds of Americans think that Trump's policies have worsened economic conditions and that his military decisions in Iran have hurt the US. Around three-quarters say the president is not in touch with the problems ordinary Americans face in their daily lives.

The latest CNN poll was conducted by SSRS from July 23-27 among a random national sample of 1,225 US adults drawn from a probability-based panel. Surveys were either conducted online or by telephone with a live interviewer. Results have a margin of sampling error of ±3.2 percentage points for the full sample, with a higher margin of error among subgroups.

Read more at the link in @cnn's bio.

📷: Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images

posts.caption:
How do you capture the essence of someone who wishes to remain anonymous?
This was one of the challenges French Algerian photographer Camille Farrah Lenain (@camille.lenain) faced as part of her series on queer Muslim life in France.
The snapshots are part of Lenain's new photobook, "Made of Smokeless Fire," released by Loose Joints Publishing.
"It's important for me to understand the people I'm photographing to the fullest," said Lenain of the six-year project which involved around 50 LGBTQ+ participants (identified by first name or initials only) from across the country.
The photos are accompanied by poetic fragments of text from several sitters on their faith, desires and memories. While some have cut off all contact with their families, others have forged fragile paths towards reconciliation. The range of experiences is as varied as the participants.
The book title refers to jinn, the supernatural creatures described in the Qur'an as "made of smokeless fire." "It's common to believe that queer Muslims are the way they are because they've been possessed by jinn, even though these entities are neither good nor bad," explained Lenain. Much like the way the word 'queer' has been reappropriated in recent years, Lenain wishes the same for LGBTQ+ Muslims and the term. "By reclaiming your own relationship to jinn, you stop giving power to others weaponizing it against you."
📸 : © Camille Farrah Lenain 2026 courtesy @jointsloose

posts.caption:
Earlier this month, @charli_xcx watched "Point Break," the 1991 action flick starring Keanu Reeves as a rookie FBI agent. It was, she said, "top to bottom the coolest everrrrr."
How do we know that? Because she logged it on Letterboxd — in an account that has become a sneak peek into a pop icon's personal artistic appetite. It's a portrait of a woman who's as likely to consume low culture ("The Idea of You," the schmaltzy Anne Hathaway boyband rom-com) as high (she gave Michelangelo Antonioni's 1960 masterpiece "L'Avventura" 5 stars).
Charli's own curation of taste and yes, coolness, stems from the reputation she's built over the years as a kind of anti-Taylor Swift, strutting on stage in massive sunglasses and knee-high boots, making dance music about key bumps and her own club adventures. She's presented herself as an alternative to the platonic ideal of a pop princess: messier, grungier, less predictable.
Her mega-successful sixth album "Brat," released in 2024, saw Charli taking that image to its neon-green extreme, channeling the hot-mess it-girls of the mid 2000s remodeled for the internet era.
Aesthetically, the version of cool on her new album "Music, Fashion, Film" is instead a blast from the pre-iPhone past. The videos released so far are all black and white, the sound stripped back. And the references liberally littered throughout "Music, Fashion, Film" demonstrate how deeply Charli values counterculture — and wants to share it with the masses.
Read more at the link in bio.
📸 : Rich Fury/Getty Images for MSG Entertainment | Brook Mitchell / AFP via Getty Images | Atlantic Records | Atlantic Records

posts.caption:
Beneath red tinsel and in the dim glow of club lighting, six young couples kiss, each seemingly wrapped up in their own little worlds. The intimate scene feels like a film still out of time, decade unclear, as they close their eyes and hold one another in the retro wood interior.
For the photographer Andrea Martí, who staged the scene inside of a vintage London nightlife hotspot, the point was for her subjects to yearn.
The image comes from the series "Everyone is Beautiful and No One is Horny," titled after the 2021 viral essay about desexed blockbuster movies led by increasingly perfect-looking leads.
"Everyone has beautiful bodies in the media, but we're seeing all these hot people and there's no tension here," Martí said. "There's no desire, yearning, anything."
She developed her series last year as part of her graduate studies at University of the Arts London. In her research, she also kept returning to the studies that say that Gen Z is having less sex, is averse to dating and is lonelier than previous generations.
Read more at the link in our bio.
📸: Andrea Martí

Some New Yorkers were able to get a closer glimpse at the trophy today at the French maison’s Fifth Avenue flagship store before it heads to the pitch this weekend.
Created in the storied workshops of Asnières-sur-Seine, near Paris, the luxe trunk is covered by the signature Louis Vuitton Monogram canvas, showcasing two front panels adorned with a golden “V” – for “Victory” and “Vuitton” – painted to pay homage to the trophy’s colors.

Enter 25-year-old Norwegian soccer player and Manchester City star @erling. Days after being knocked out of the World Cup quarter-finals by England, Haaland and his partner Isabel Haugseng Johansen dusted themselves off and headed to the Mediterranean for the @dolcegabbana Alta Sartoria show in Sicily on Tuesday.
Haaland, who has already caught the world's attention with his sprawling collection of Hermès bags and relatable love for a tacky trinket, was dressed to the nines.
He clashed his cream satin pants with a white double-breasted blazer, dark sunshades, a gold frog-shaped brooch and navy woven leather loafers. Most notable was his thin satin-like scarf whipped eccentrically over one shoulder, like a Milanese gentleman oozing sprezzatura.

posts.caption:
At the turn of the millennium, Berlin had become one of Europe’s most exciting cultural capitals. Artists, musicians, designers and photographers were drawn to the city, transforming it into a place where creativity flourished and new ideas shaped the decade ahead. It was the perfect backdrop for an editorial that explored fashion through the lens of a city constantly reinventing itself.
Photographed by Inez van Lamsweerde & Vinoodh Matadin, Berlin’s New Wave follows Kate Moss through Berlin’s streets, modern architecture and remnants of its divided past. The wardrobe reflects that same balance of history and change. Sharp tailoring, oversized tweed coats, military-inspired jackets and sculptural outerwear are paired with sheer tights, silk blouses, bold prints and rich textures, creating looks that feel elegant without losing their edge.
The city becomes more than a location. Graffiti-covered walls, post-war buildings and newly emerging districts give the editorial a sense of movement, capturing Berlin at a time when it was redefining its cultural identity. Fashion and the city evolve together, each reinforcing the other’s character.
More than twenty years later, the editorial still feels remarkably current. The oversized tailoring, refined outerwear and confident silhouettes that run through the story continue to influence fashion today, proving that some editorials don’t simply capture a moment, they anticipate what comes next.
Editorial: Berlin’s New Wave
Magazine: Harper’s Bazaar US — September 2000
Model: Kate Moss
Photography: Inez van Lamsweerde & Vinoodh Matadin
Fashion Editor: Brana Wolf
posts.alt_text:
Looking back at Pull & Bear’s 2008 catalogue, it’s hard not to notice how much of it feels relevant again. The collection captured the effortless, indie-inspired style that was everywhere at the time.

The wardrobe revolved around skinny jeans, striped knitwear, graphic tees, mini dresses, checked shirts and military jackets, paired with oversized scarves, knee-high boots and fitted pea coats. Every look had the ease of clothes that had been thrown together rather than carefully planned, giving the catalogue a sense of authenticity that still resonates today.

Photographed across the streets of Berlin, the campaign reflected a generation shaped by live music, nights out and everyday city life. There was no obsession with perfection or quiet luxury, just youthful silhouettes, layered basics and an effortless confidence that came naturally.

Nearly two decades later, many of those same pieces have returned to fashion almost unchanged. Looking through the catalogue today, it’s clear that they really knew what they were doing in 2008.

Credits 
Brand : Pull & Bear
Model : Vlada Roslyakova

posts.caption:
When Steven Meisel photographs a celebrity, the result is rarely just a portrait. His images have a way of dissolving the line between fashion and character, and with Timothée Chalamet, he found a subject equally committed to transformation. Together, they created an editorial that felt less like a celebrity shoot and more like a study of modern masculinity through the language of fashion.
Chalamet moved effortlessly between leather, sheer fabrics, pearls and sculptural silhouettes. Styled by Edward Enninful, the editorial rejected convention in favour of individuality, drawing from houses including Rick Owens, Prada, Balmain, Mugler, Versace, Haider Ackermann and Louis Vuitton.
Published as the cover story for British Vogue’s October 2022 issue, the editorial marked a historic moment, with Chalamet becoming the first man to appear alone on the magazine’s cover in its 106-year history. More importantly, it reinforced what had already become clear: Timothée Chalamet wasn’t simply wearing fashion, he had become one of its defining faces.
Publication:British Vogue — October 2022
Photography:Steven Meisel
Fashion Editor / Styling:Edward Enninful
Hair:Guido Palau
Makeup:Pat McGrath
Manicure:Jin Soon Choi

posts.caption:
Throughout the late 2000s and early 2010s, few models were as consistently present on the runway as Vlada Roslyakova. With her instantly recognisable features, effortless versatility and distinctive runway presence, she became one of fashion’s most in-demand faces, walking for virtually every major luxury house and establishing herself as one of the industry’s most booked models.
After making her international breakthrough in 2005, Roslyakova’s career quickly gained momentum. Season after season, she appeared in an extraordinary number of shows, working with Chanel, Dior, Prada, Louis Vuitton, Valentino, Givenchy, Alexander McQueen, Balenciaga, Versace and Jean Paul Gaultier. At the peak of her career, she was widely regarded as one of the most booked models in fashion, becoming a defining face of the era’s runway circuit.
Away from the catwalk, Roslyakova built an equally impressive editorial career. She appeared in the pages of Vogue, i-D, Numéro, W, Dazed and countless international fashion publications, photographed by industry legends including Steven Meisel, David Sims, Craig McDean, Mert & Marcus, Peter Lindbergh and Patrick Demarchelier.
Nearly two decades after her debut, Vlada Roslyakova remains one of the defining models of her generation. Her extensive body of work and remarkable consistency made her not only one of the most recognisable faces of the 2000s, but also one of the busiest and most enduring models of the decade.

posts.caption:
When Hedi Slimane unveiled his first women’s collection for the newly renamed Saint Laurent in Spring 2013, it signalled the beginning of a new era. From the house’s rebranding to its unmistakable rock-and-roll attitude, Slimane introduced a vision that would redefine Saint Laurent for an entire generation.
Rather than recreating Yves Saint Laurent’s archives, Slimane translated the house through his own lens. Sharp black tailoring, floor-length capes, sheer blouses, slouchy hats and glittering evening jackets were infused with the effortless cool that had become synonymous with his work. References to Betty Catroux, 1970s Paris and the Los Angeles music scene merged into a collection that felt both nostalgic and unmistakably contemporary.
The collection divided critics almost immediately. Some questioned Slimane’s radical departure from recent Saint Laurent history, while others praised his ability to capture the rebellious spirit that had always existed within the house. Time would ultimately prove its influence. The silhouettes, attitude and rock-inspired aesthetic shaped not only Saint Laurent’s identity throughout the 2010s, but also the wider direction of luxury fashion.
More than a decade later, Hedi Slimane’s debut remains one of the most defining runway moments of the century—a collection that challenged expectations and forever changed the visual language of Saint Laurent.

posts.caption:
Some careers are remembered through albums. Lady Gaga’s can just as easily be traced through the clothes she wore. Every era came with a new visual identity, each look carefully constructed to challenge expectations and push fashion beyond the red carpet. What could have been publicity stunts became some of the defining images of 21st-century fashion.
At the 2009 MTV Video Music Awards, Gaga introduced a new kind of celebrity dressing in a series of theatrical Alexander McQueen looks, proving that fashion could be just as unforgettable as the performance itself. A year later, she delivered one of pop culture’s most iconic fashion moments in the Meat Dress, designed by Franc Fernandez and styled by Nicola Formichetti. Instantly controversial, it became one of the most discussed garments ever worn on a red carpet.
For the 2011 Grammy Awards, Gaga arrived inside a translucent egg before emerging to perform Born This Way, turning an entrance into performance art. Around the same time, her collaboration with Nicola Formichetti helped relaunch Mugler, introducing the house’s sharp silhouettes and futuristic glamour to a new generation.
Her love for couture found another perfect match in John Galliano, whose dramatic creations echoed Gaga’s fascination with fashion as storytelling. Whether wearing Galliano, McQueen or Mugler, she approached clothing not simply as something to wear, but as a way of building characters.
Even moments of royal protocol became unforgettable. During the 2009 Royal Variety Performance, Gaga performed before Queen Elizabeth II in a sculptural scarlet gown by Atelier Versace, creating one of the most memorable fashion moments ever witnessed by the British monarchy.
More than fifteen years later, these appearances continue to shape conversations around celebrity style. They weren’t simply iconic outfits—they helped redefine what fashion could look like when performance, identity and couture became impossible to separate.

posts.caption:
Five Palestine Action activists, between the ages of 28 and 70, face being sentenced as terrorists after they spray-painted and cracked the windows of a Barclays bank in Lancashire. ⁠
⁠
They were protesting the company for its alleged financial links to Elbit Systems, Israel’s largest arms manufacturer. ⁠
⁠
Last month, activists Brendon O’Hagan, Amanda Kelly, Hmeera Atiqnisar, Mohammed Malik, and Alma Yaniv were found guilty of causing £212,000 in damage during the action. ⁠
⁠
It was only after the verdict that Judge Phillip Parry told the prosecution and defence that he intended to consider a “terrorist connection” in the sentencing, even though the jury and the defendants had not previously been informed that this was a possibility.⁠
⁠
Last month, the Filton 4 were the first protesters in Britain to be sentenced as terrorists without being convicted of terror offences, with sentences ranging from four to eight years.⁠
⁠
Amnesty International have said that these terrorist sentences mark a ‘dangerous’ move against the right to protest in the UK. ⁠
⁠
#palestineaction #news #ukpolitics⁠

In coordinated Instagram story posts this morning, all seven members of @bts.bighitofficial confirmed that will not be submitting their music for Grammys consideration this year.
⁠
The move is likely a response to the Grammys’ introduction of the new Best Asian Pop Music Performance category at the next ceremony, which has been criticised for pigeon-holing Asian artists.⁠
⁠
BTS are the first and only K-Pop group to receive Grammy nods — including three Best Pop Duo/Group Performance nominations. Their latest album, Arirang, meanwhile, currently holds the record for most-streamed album of 2026.⁠
⁠
Elsewhere, the 69th Grammy Awards, taking place February 2027, will also include new categories for Best Latin Song and Best RnB Solo Performance.⁠

posts.caption:
In a viral joint statement shared Wednesday, BTS announced they won’t be submitting their hit comeback album ‘Arirang’ for 2027 Grammys consideration. The announcement comes just weeks after the Recording Academy unveiled a new Best Asian Pop Music category, which immediately raised eyebrows online.
“We hope music itself can be heard and loved rather than being distinguished by region or language,” the K-pop group posted online in Korean. “We thank Army and everyone who has always stood by us.”
The Grammys add new categories every few years, but lately some additions are looking extra sus. After Beyoncé made history by winning both AOTY and Best Country Album for ‘Cowboy Carter,’ the Academy suddenly split its country categories into Contemporary and Traditional. Interesting timing 🤔
Earlier this year, Bad Bunny’s ‘Debí Tirar Más Fotos’ became the first Spanish-language album to win AOTY and suddenly the Recording Academy is rolling out a Best Latin Song category for 2027…
BTS has performed at the Grammys three times, with “Butter” becoming the most-watched Grammy performance ever on YouTube. The group has also earned five Grammy nominations and still has yet to win any.
Although BTS would’ve been a major contender to win the first Best Asian Pop Music award, they’re making a statement by choosing to opt out entirely. And if anyone’s taking the L here, it’s probably the Grammys, who just lost their biggest engagement magnet before the category even debuted. Too bad.
Anyway... congrats to BTS on the sold-out world tour!
#bts #kpop #music #grammys #news

posts.caption:
Trump mentioned Dylan Mulvaney not once, not twice, but four times during his White House Correspondents’ Dinner Speech on Friday, which was rescheduled after a gunman purportedly opened fire on the event in April.
The eyeroll-inducing statement happened while he singled out CNN’s Kaitlan Collins, who was in attendance to accept an award for her coverage of the White House. “She’s a young, attractive woman. She never smiles,” the president stated. Trump has repeatedly criticized Collins for “not smiling” during his second term.
He then compared Collins to Mulvaney in an attempt to make a joke. “I thought Kaitlan had really made it big with a major new sponsorship, but then I informed her that it wasn’t her on the Bud Light can, it was Dylan Mulvaney,” Trump said, referencing Mulvaney’s three-year-old ad campaign. On Sunday, Trump doubled down on Truth Social, posting an AI-generated image of Collins’ face on Mulvaney’s body.
Mulvaney, meanwhile, seemed largely unbothered. She said she was “incredibly honored” to be compared to Collins before dragging the president.
“It seems to me that I might be the one that got away for these men, like I am permanently burned into their retinas, I am microchipped into their minds,” she said. “Being publicly mocked and criticized by this administration is actually, like, the greatest compliment of all.”
She then questioned why she seems to live rent-free in MAGA’s minds. “Why is it so important to them that I don’t find success?... Oh my God... freedom! I am free in a way that they will never have the privilege to experience, and they want to use their power to take away my freedom.” she said.
“But what they don’t understand is my freedom has zero contingency on what they can provide for me, because my freedom is fully dependent on the moment that I acknowledged my real, authentic self.”
Mulvaney ended by urging viewers to support trans and nonbinary people, closing with a pointed message for Trump: “To the president, thank you for reminding me that I am more powerful than I even knew.”

posts.caption:
This week, Anthea M. Hartig, the director of Smithsonian National Museum of American History, endured a congressional hearing by GOP lawmakers who believe the museum is not quite patriotic enough to properly represent the USA. The hearing came after the White House released a 160-page report on July 4th titled “Saving America’s Story” decrying the Smithsonian’s focus on white supremacy and systemic injustice.
Owing to the ignorance of the GOP lawmaker’s questions, Texas Democratic congresswoman Jasmine Crockett called the event a “white pride rally disguised as a congressional hearing.”
At the hearing, Texas Republican congressman Brandon Gill focused specifically on gift shop merchandise that featured a “Latina Power” slogan.
“Do you think that it’s appropriate for the Smithsonian Institution to sell ‘Latina Power’ paraphernalia?” Gill asked.
Hartig refused to dumb her response down to “yes or no” despite Gill’s insistence that she answer that way. Assumedly, for Gill, the question of whether a museum should promote ‘Latina Power’ was as simple as whether it should also promote other kinds of racial/gendered power; white male power, for example.
But for Hartig, an award-winning historian and the first woman to hold her role at the Smithsonian, the question was likely too reductive for “yes or no” to suffice, perhaps owing to the white supremacy and systemic injustice which disempowers Latina women in the first place. But that’s just a guess, as Gill didn’t actually allow her to answer the question.
Another wild moment that took place during the hearing included a tirade against sexually explicit transgender ideology. Representative Nancy Mace, who spearheaded the issue, showed images of Rupaul while asking Hartig:
“Do you believe men can become women?”
Hartig attempted to explain that the line of questioning was irrelevant to the hearing and also that Rupaul himself is not transgender, but Mace, like Gill, did not allow her to answer.
In her closing statements, Hartig invited the GOP lawmakers to walk the Smithsonian with her sometime. Maybe it would do them some good to study up on American history with one of our country’s leading experts?

posts.caption:
While Chanel is enjoying a stellar revitalization via Matthieu Blazy, the company is still not immune to the nightmares which have long plagued luxury fashion. First, a criminal trial taking place in Hong Kong has exposed Chanel’s history of destroying huge quantities of unsold products. Second, Chanel was recently raided by Italian authorities under suspicion of labor exploitation in their supply chain.
Product destruction has been a highly controversial practice among luxury brands for years. And last week, China began the criminal trial of two former Chanel employees who in 2017 conspired to steal 724 bags and wallets slated for destruction. Shockingly, the trial has revealed that Chanel was, at the time, destroying 10k-20k products every six months.
It’s difficult to imagine participating in that level of waste as a warehouse worker, knowing the steep profits that could come from selling them illegally. The employees were caught on camera boxing up the merchandise, and were later apprehended loading the boxes into vehicles.
Coincidentally, just this weekend, an EU ban on product destruction went into effect. Chanel claims to have long ceased product-destruction and insists that the information coming out of Hong Kong does not reflect their current business practices.
Meanwhile, in Italy, a myriad of high-fashion firms including Chanel, Brunello Cucinelli, and Moncler were raided last week by Italian authorities under suspicion of labor exploitation. The brands are not yet under formal investigation, but were found to have worked with two subcontractors that provided garment bags and shopping bags, whose working conditions were “demeaning” and unsafe.
Chanel reportedly was made aware of the potential labor abuse in May, and instructed their suppliers to sever business ties with the subcontractors. Now, they are fully cooperating with the Italian authorities.
It looks like Chanel is working to make things right. But, exploitation and destructive practices have been part of the luxury market for years. It’ll take a long time to reconcile that, no matter how determined or altruistic companies like Chanel may be.

posts.caption:
Pardon my French, but in couture’s endless game of who did it first?, let’s talk about who actually did it first. That would be Ritu Beri.
A protégée of embroidery maestro François Lesage, she became the first Indian designer invited as a guest designer on the Haute Couture calendar. She is, and always will be, THAT girl. Very First Lady of the Universe-coded.
On 17 July 1999, she presented her debut couture collection (Fall 1999/2000) at the Indian Embassy in Paris, a venue that would go on to become the backdrop for several of her shows. Behind the runway sat the now-famous Padmapani mural from the Ajanta caves. Twenty-seven years later, the same mural has the girls (grown men) fighting. Foreshadowing? Perhaps. Mrs. Beri has always possessed a curious kind of clairvoyance, the ability to spot the future of Indian fashion and arrive there before anyone else even knew the destination.
The funds were scarce. Even the models had no shoes, only feet dyed in blood-red alta. But this was an era when fashion fairy tales still had a little magic left in them. Hope and audacity could still outrun reality. Unknown designers could still assemble guest lists that included Suzy Menkes, who would go on to rave about Beri in the International Herald Tribune. Those bare red feet became symbols of sensuality. The saris and dresses were hypnotic. The audience was captivated.
Until then, the idea of India in fashion had largely been interpreted through European designers and legacy maisons. This was one of the first moments an Indian designer seized control of the lens through which the Indian story would be told. So now, while everyone wants to be the blueprint, we’re forgetting who first paved the road from Delhi to Paris. Whose ateliers cracked open the couture calendar and made space for the generations of Indian designers who followed.
In an exclusive tête-à-tête with DS, Miss ma’am Beri reflects on the realities of being first, the costs, the courage, and the satisfaction of making history.
Images: Ritu Beri, Spring 2000 Haute Couture.

#ELLECoverStar: Twelve years into her career, success has made Kriti Sanon (@kritisanon) more fearless, but not careless. “I have to instinctively feel that this is something I can’t let go of,” she says. The old fear of needing to constantly be on set has faded, replaced by a simple shift: “It is more about quality versus quantity now.”
For our Luxury Issue, that idea feels especially relevant. Luxury, at its most meaningful, isn’t only about access, but discernment: the ability to choose fewer, better things, and to pause without mistaking stillness for disappearance. Sanon doesn’t speak of this phase as though she’s arrived. “This is probably the most exciting phase of my life and my career so far,” she says, with gratitude in her voice — and relief, too.
Click the 🔗 in bio to read the complete interview.

posts.caption:
Welcome to the next era of @karolg.
Following her historic Coachella performance in April—where she became the first Latina to headline the annual music festival—the Grammy-winning Colombian pop star has been rehearsing endlessly for her biggest international stadium tour yet: Viajando por el Mundo Tropitour. Following her previous Mañana Será Bonito tour—the fifth-highest-grossing tour by a Latin artist of all time—her new show will be both a celebration of the Latin community and an expansion of her sound and performance. “People try to pigeonhole me, but I’m so many things,” she tells ELLE. “I love that my image and what I represent are deeply Latin, yet I also want to be a global artist.”
In ELLE’s Summer 2026 digital cover story, the global superstar opens up about her pride in representing the Latin community, finding herself through love and loss, and teases her next musical era: “The next version of me will be new to people, but it’s always been there.”
Read the full interview at the link in bio.

Editor-in-chief: Nina Garcia @ninagarcia
Photographer: Elliot and Erick Jiménez @elliotanderick
Stylist: Nycole Sariol @nycolesariol

posts.alt_text:
Presenting our first of four Summer Issue cover stars, @annehathaway.

Due to filming and release delays, Hathaway now has five movies premiering within six months. Her insanely busy year continues with her starring role as Penelope in @theodysseymovie. (To which she says: “It’s crazy to have four years of work coming out in six months.”) After weathering the storms of Hollywood, the in-demand star is finally collecting her flowers—and stopping to smell them. “If I’m not enjoying it, then really, really what’s wrong with me?” she tells ELLE. “If I can’t have a positive outlook on it when I’m having such a fortunate ride, then it would be wasted on me.”

For ELLE’s Summer 2026 issue, Hathaway reflects on how she’s grown since the early days of her career, reuniting with Christopher Nolan after 12 years, and navigating online criticism: “We’re at a time when people feel very confident in assuming what they think is fact.” Read the full cover story at the link in bio.

posts.caption:
As a mother of two, WNBA All-Star Weekend looks a little different for @breannastewart30 these days. Though her wife, @martaxargay, and kids—Ruby, 4, and Theo, 2—have been accompanying the @nyliberty star to All-Star Weekends for years now, Stewart says this one was extra special.
The highlight of her weekend? Stepping out in their “first nice family fit.” On Thursday night, Stewart, Xargay Casademont, and the kids wore coordinated black, blue, and white striped outfits, with selects from @off____white, @publicschoolnyc, and @acnestudios. It’s a milestone in Stewart’s personal style journey, which has been constantly evolving since 2019. “That’s when I really found out what I liked—the brands that I like, how I want my clothes to be fitting—oversized sometimes, but I also can wear high-waisted and tiny tees too,” she tells ELLE. “I would describe my personal style is just fitted basically. Tailored. Put together.”
Swipe through for a glimpse into Stewart’s All-Star weekend photo diary—and tap the link in bio for the full look.

posts.caption:
“Hi Shakaila we’re xyz producers and we’d love to make a tv show with you” I’ve had a handful of those conversations over the years and they quickly go from 🤩 to 🫩
I used to feel disheartened until I looked around and saw so many examples of people not waiting for permission and instead deciding to get up and make shit happen! So that’s what I decided to do, turn this decades long dream into a reality! I pulled in every favour I had! Turned my friends into producers and show runners, begged and borrowed and you know what, it turned out pretty damn good if I do say so myself 😅
This black history month especially, I’m inspired by the talented Black British women who have shown me that it’s possible to make a mark on the small screen no matter the limitations!
I absolutely loved makeover shows growing up! But as I got older I saw how they were more brutal than beautiful!
Today, fashion psychology shows us just how deeply our clothes impact our mental health, identity, and confidence.
That’s why I’m so excited to share The Wearapy Show my new makeover series that blends fashion psychology, emotional healing and real style transformations.
We help everyday people reclaim their wardrobes after major life shifts: grief, motherhood, identity struggles, and more.
With a team of experts and no judgment, just science-backed guidance and love.
Episodes 1 and 2 launch 26th October on the Fashion is Psychology YouTube Channel. Subscribe now and follow the journey.
#bhm #wearapy #fashionpsychology #makeover

posts.caption:
Where do high street brands fall as far as availability and ethics? We mapped them, to help visualize the solution 🤓⁠
⁠
In plotting brands by how well or poorly they rate by our ratings methodology and how available they are, the results made clear something we talk and talk and talk about: smaller brands are more likely to be more sustainable, by taking on measures like adopting circularity initiatives, committing to lower impact fibres, and paying workers fairly.⁠
⁠
Look to the top left as proof, where so many “Good” rated but less-available brands (Sweden’s @asket, Australia’s @spell, France’s @veja, the US’ @reformation) land in comparison to the bottom right, where brands that rate our three lowest of “It’s a Start” through “We Avoid” land: they're all mega-corporations with global availability (adidas, Nike, MAC, H&M, Lacoste, Zara, SHEIN), brands that are profiting the most but doing the least.⁠
⁠
At the other end, smaller and lower rated brands (Malin+Goetz, Sézane, J.Crew) show that there’s always room to grow at any size while bigger and higher rated brands (Aesop, Lush, The North Face) illustrate how change *is* possible.⁠
⁠
Note the lone “Great”—our highest rating—is @nudiejeans, which has remarkable ethics and availability. That’s what brands should strive for, and is proof brands can work better for people, the planet, and animals should they commit to working transparently 💚⁠
⁠
Where would your favourite brand fall on this grid? Which should we map next? Share in the comments, then visit the link to explore brand ratings at the link ↑⁠
⁠
#Fashion #Shopping #SustainableFashion #Sustainability #FashionTech
posts.alt_text:
Gap has gotten in a bit of trouble for rereleasing a collection from the 2000s. Any guesses what the drama is about? 🤔⁠
⁠
Turns out, the brand’s rerelease pivots garments from cotton to polyester—and people are calling the brand out, for using the material and for creating clothes in the style of ultra fast fashion brands like SHEIN and Temu 😶‍🌫️⁠
⁠
These critiques are correct, but there’s something else that seems to be missing: Gap is a fast fashion brand. While designer collaborations and stunts like this build buzz, they’re closer to SHEIN than one might think.⁠
⁠
Swipe to explore the reaction, how Gap rates, and alternatives to patterned clothing from “Good” and “Great” brands. What are your thoughts on this? Share in the comments, then visit the link for recommendations of brands that embrace patterns ↑⁠
⁠
📸 Zac Posen⁠
⁠
#Gap #GapStudio #Shopping #SummerStyles #Sustainability

posts.caption:
HUGE NEWS: Good On You has officially rated over 7,000 brands 🎉 This is a major accomplishment, as even more brands—from the small and indie through the large and luxury—are in our Directory.⁠
⁠
What goes into ratings? 🤔 A lot, actually: we have a rigorous, comprehensive system analysing up to 1,000 data points across 100 key issues to arrive at our lowest score (“We Avoid”) to our highest score (“Great”). Ratings are based solely on a brand’s transparent, public reporting that we pair with credible third-party indices, certifications, and standards.⁠
⁠
How do we select brands to rate? Well…with your help 🥹 Many of our ratings come through community requests, shared in comments and messages, which helps us understand which brands to prioritise to meet this moment. Additionally, our retail and ecommerce partners along with brands request ratings too, which is a key means to apply change to the industry from within.⁠
⁠
Another item to celebrate here? Of these rated brands, 1,000 have received our two highest scores, “Good” and “Great”. This is very exciting news, representative of how more brands are doing considering their impact on workers, the planet, and animals. (Even if that also means…6000 brands have a lot more to do to reduce their impact.)⁠
⁠
Here’s to continuing to keep people like you informed while supporting more sustainable brands that are making the difference! Cheers 🥂 Explore our 7,000 ratings at the link too ✨⁠
⁠
#SustainableFashion #FastFashion #ConsciousConsumer #EthicalConsumer #SustainableStyle #ConsciousStyle #GoodOnYou #GoodOnYouApp #EthicalFashion⁠

posts.caption:
Presenting one of our three Summer issue covers with the leading men of @theodysseymovie: Matt Damon as Odysseus.
A Hollywood veteran of nearly five decades now, Damon has worked on approximately 80 film sets. And yet, as he told GQ’s @zachbaron, “Every single location on this movie would’ve been the hardest location on any other movie I’ve ever done… Every time we’d go somewhere, we’d be like, ‘Well, Iceland will be easier.’ And then it’s raining sideways and it’s fucking freezing. Iceland was like, ‘Yeah, easy? Hey, hold my beer.’”
For Damon, though, the challenge was part of what made the project so special: “All of the things that might have been difficult for me at an earlier point in my life weren’t difficult. They became fun. Like being wet and cold was not a hardship. It was actually something I felt really lucky to be experiencing. It felt temporary and like a gift.”
Damon unwraps the ‘gift’ that was making The Odyssey, alongside his co-stars Robert Pattinson and Tom Holland, and director Christopher Nolan, for GQ’s summer issue cover story at the 🔗 in bio.

Presenting one of our three Summer issue covers with the leading men of @theodysseymovie: Robert Pattinson as Antinous. 

Pattinson’s part in The Odyssey is not big—he plays the cockiest of the many suitors who have installed themselves at Ithaca, seeking the hand of Penelope (played by Anne Hathaway) while Matt Damon’s Odysseus is away. “My character’s a little like James Woods in Casino. That was my inspiration for it,” Pattinson said. “He’s like a little sleazy. I kept saying at my costume fitting, ‘I really want to have leopard underpants.’”

Pattinson talks to GQ’s @zachbaron about teaming up with Nolan again for The Odyssey, alongside co-stars Matt Damon and Tom Holland, at the 🔗 in bio.

posts.caption:
Presenting one of our three Summer issue covers with the leading men of @theodysseymovie: Tom Holland as Telemachus.
When Christopher Nolan first offered Holland a part in The Odyssey, the production dates were identical to those of Spider-Man: Brand New Day (and Holland’s commitments to the Spider-Man franchise are ironclad). “I said to Chris, like, ‘Look, I want to do this movie, but if I’m going to do it, I’m going to have to call Sony and have a very uncomfortable conversation,’ ” Holland said. Then he immediately had a very uncomfortable conversation.
“Chris has that reputation of ‘This movie isn’t going to go five months over, and we aren’t actually going to lose Tom for two years,’ ” Holland said. “Any other director, it might have been a slightly different conversation.” The Odyssey started on the day Nolan said it would and finished nine days early.
For our summer cover story, Holland talks about coming of age on set, getting to star alongside his partner on another project, and how he’s approaching the future of his career at the 🔗 in bio.

Like mother, like daughter ✨
When your mother is a 90s icon and ex-supermodel, it would be rude not to take inspo from her archival wardrobe. And that’s certainly what Kaia Gerber has done with her latest look, and she looks the spitting image of her mum, Cindy Crawford.
Whilst promoting her new show, The Shards, Gerber stepped out onto the streets of New York City wearing almost the exact same black slip dress Crawford wore to the premiere of A League of Their Own, back in 1992.
Gerber paired her slinky, floor-sweeping dress with a lightweight scarf draped around her neck and a pair of Tom Ford sunglasses, opting for a modern take on her mother’s signature go-to silhouette.

posts.caption:
@thefamousgregjackson doesn’t just design clothes. He designs the life they’ll live in.
“If I haven’t worn something in a year, I’ll always sell it because I’m trying to have a small closet.”
The @greglaboratory founder approaches his wardrobe the same way he approaches his brand, every piece has to earn its place. That means signed Jun Takahashi jackets, a regrettably sold Yohji Yamamoto trench, a @Cartier Santos bought in the “wrong” size, and enough @BjornQorn popcorn to keep a fancy grocery store in business.
Read more about the designer’s favorite things at the link on our story.
By: Maximilian Migowski
posts.alt_text:
Introducing our final cover star of the spring issue of HIGHSNOBIETY, @kaytranada. Kay is the type of artist that just gets you off your feet, whose beats take you through the movement. His success has amounted to Grammys, collaborations with artists such as @kaliuchis, and a change to the whole electronic scene. 

What comes as a surprise is that it was all a “happy accident,” as the artist puts it. Kay’s real passion lay in the creation of dark and moody sample-driven hip-hop. Montreal shit, as he so succinctly put it — and the very music he grew up with.  We spoke to Kaytranda about his journey, and how he’s ready to go back to his roots and burrow into the underground with plans to drop “Mixtapes, beat tapes, EPs.” Kaytranada will be here: tinkering, listening, conjuring something unlike anything that came before.   

Read more about Kay and how he’s doing things his own way at the link in bio. 

By @pxthompson

posts.caption:
Think of the most fashionable sport in the world right now. It’s soccer, isn’t it? The beautiful game has been a catalyst for some of fashion’s biggest trends and moments over the last few years, but that dominance in our sartorial culture could be waning.
In the months leading up to the 2026 World Cup, soccer has been inescapable on the fashion front. Jerseys, sneakers, tracksuits and collaborations have had everyone in a footy state of mind, but “World Cup fatigue” in America might be basketball’s entry point to stake it’s claim as the most fashionable sport in the world right now.
While blokecore brought the beautiful game to the world, particularly the States, it seems it’s America’s turn to share one of its greatest sporting exports with the fashion scene. We looked at the rise of basketball as a style behemoth and the changing of the sporty fashion guard. Head to the link in bio to read the full story.
Images: Courtesy of brands, Getty Images

For most artists, some records are about reinvention. @syd's latest album 'Beard' is about owning the sound she's built and honed.⁠
⁠
For our latest digital cover, Hypebeast sits down with Syd to discuss her third solo album and the experiences that shaped its perspective. From finally buying a home and renovating her studio, to intentionally defining the sonic line between her solo work and @theinternet, the cover story captures an artist who has stopped chasing the next milestone and started embracing the ones she's already reached.⁠
⁠

⁠

⁠

⁠
Head to the link in bio to read our latest digital cover story and learn how those ideas shaped not only 'Beard,' but the life Syd has spent years building.⁠

posts.caption:
Suburban New Jersey isn’t the first place you’d expect to see @champagnepapi posted up for a week, but if there’s one thing about Drake he’s going to surprise us with something absolutely none of us had on our radar.
Less than 24 hours after the FIFA World Cup Finals match went down in East Rutherford, New Jersey, the rapper headed just about 40 miles west to the Garden State’s Somerset County, where he set up shop at the sprawling, roughly 500-acre Pendry Natirar estate for his second annual NOCTA Manor retreat.
A multisensory collision of the albums’ storytelling with NOCTA touchpoints, the Manor marked an immersive merging of sport, music, and fashion, with a myriad of today’s tastemakers from across the cultural zeitgeist checking in for a stay.
From the custom gear and goodie bags (complete with the “Shabang” slippers) to the guest list and golf carts, read more at the link in bio.

BTS’ @rkive is bringing his personal art collection to @sfmoma.⁠
⁠
Titled 'RM x SFMOMA: Between You and Me,' the exhibition brings Korean modern and contemporary art into dialogue with the museum’s holdings, offering a closer look at the artists and ideas that have shaped RM beyond music.⁠
⁠
The 200-work presentation will feature pieces from his collection by Yun Hyong-keun, Park Rehyun, Kwon Okyon, Kim Yun Shin, To Sangbong and Chang Ucchin, among others.⁠
⁠
Opening October 3, 2026. Read more via the link in bio.⁠
⁠
Credit: @sfmoma

posts.caption:
Sahher Bambba (@sahherbambba) is exactly where she’s always wanted to be. From landing her breakthrough role as the unapologetic Karishma Talwar in The Ba**ds of Bollywood to navigating the entertainment industry as an outsider, she believes that what’s meant for her will always find its way. There’s an undeniable energy about her, and we got a glimpse of it during our latest cover shoot.
For our latest Youthquake cover, amidst LSA's official food month, Sahher joined us for a midnight adventure at a sparkly convenience store, where she was quite literally like a kid in a candy store. One moment, she’s climbing into a shopping cart; the next, she’s turning up the heat in the frozen section. Her infectious joy is impossible to miss.
Read the full cover story at the link in our bio.

Episode 2 of Inside View Season 2, by Architecture+Design (@architectureplusdesign.in) and Lifestyle Asia India (@lifestyleasiaindia), powered by Schueco India (@schueco__india), is a conversation that brings together design, performance, and lived experience in a deeply engaging way. ‘Spaces That Breathe & Flow ‘dissects how architecture, movement, and the body come together to shape the spaces we inhabit.
Featuring architects Siddarth G. Sankar (@sankar_and_associates, @siddu1975) and Prasanna Parvatikar (@cubism_architects, @architect_prasanna), alongside dancer, choreographer, and cultural commentator Anita Ratnam (@anitaratnam.official), the conversation unfolds around rehearsal, threshold, instinct, and performance spaces that allow both the body and the imagination to breathe.
Coming soon!

posts.caption:
#LSASociety: For the inaugural event of LSA Society, Lifestyle Asia India in association with Interio by Godrej (@interiobygodrej), brought together acclaimed chef, author, restaurateur and culinary director of Avas Wellness, Suvir Saran (@suvirsaran) and his longtime mentee, Chef Hari (@haridashvmalhotra), for an evening of storytelling, cooking, and shared learning. Through an interactive masterclass and tasting, the duo presented their unique rendition of the iconic butter chicken, with the dish reflecting the evolution of a mentor and mentee working side by side.
Inspired by the spirit of a jugalbandi, the evening explored how tradition is kept alive through collaboration. As Chef Suvir shared decades of culinary wisdom, Chef Hari brought fresh perspectives and fearless curiosity, creating a dialogue that extended beyond the kitchen. More than a masterclass, it was a celebration of mentorship, friendship, and the idea that the best meals, like the best relationships, are built through conversation.
[Lifestyle Asia India, LSA Society, Interio by Godrej, Chef Suvir Saran, Chef Hari, culinary masterclass]

posts.caption:
Introducing our global cover star, @TravisScott!
The Houston-born artist has spent the past year moving between worlds, crafting the follow-up to 2023’s ‘Utopia’ from his Malibu studio while preparing for his much-anticipated acting debut as a bard in Christopher Nolan’s @theodysseymovie, in theaters July 17.
From music to film to fashion, Scott’s creative universe continues to expand. He also stars alongside Owen Wilson in the upcoming comedy ‘Rolling Loud’ and maintains long-running partnerships with @Nike and @Oakley, all while leading @cactusjack into its next chapter.
Yet at the center of it all remains the music. “I’ve been mad inspired over the last year and a half,” Scott says. “I’ve been buckled down and back building beats from scratch, just creating and pushing the sound.”
Read our full cover story at the link in bio as Scott opens up about the creative forces that drive him, his big-screen debut, and the importance of self-care.

@francesca.scorsese grew up immersed in cinema, raised on films by her father, legendary director @martinscorsese_. “He kept a log of every film he showed me—what day it was, how old I was, where we were,” she tells L’OFFICIEL.
After graduating from NYU Tisch in 2023, the actor and filmmaker directed two shorts, ‘Crimson Ties’ and ‘Fish Out of Water;’ she’s now developing ‘Adults Only,’ a dark comedy inspired by her mother. A natural observer, Scorsese has also cultivated a passion for photography, capturing quiet moments away from the spotlight. For our July/August 2026 issue, she opens her archive, sharing intimate photographs taken on her Contax T2. “There are so many sentimental photos of my parents,” she says. “Just quiet moments people normally wouldn’t see.”
Carrying one of cinema’s most iconic legacies has shaped Scorsese’s journey in its own complicated ways. Reflecting on the weight—and privilege—of her name, she says: “I feel like I have this shadow over me, but in the best way. My name opens doors for me, but it also closes a lot of them. It’s a bit of a mindfuck, but it’s something I can’t escape.” Read more from Francesca Scorsese at the link in bio.
Writer @samanthajsimon
Photos courtesy of @dev.baby and @francesca.scorsese

When your favorite artist announces that they are going on tour, do you scramble to find an outfit that fits within its visual universe, simply rock their merchandise, or decide not to follow the theme at all? Before the age of the Internet, one would simply buy a ticket, throw on a band tee, and jam out to an artist’s live set.
However, with rising costs that have impacted ticket sales, the experience has turned into an occasion to go all out for. And thanks to social media, the ways that we dress for a concert, performance, or festival have been elevated to the max.
From the friendship bracelets that took over @taylorswift’s #ErasTour to @chappellroan’s distinct themes at each stop during her ‘Rise and Fall of a Midwest Princess’ tour, artists know the impact their music has on their fans, and fashion is the ultimate method to unite. Read more on the rise of the concert uniform at the link in our bio.

#ManifestCover
Two years into marriage, nine into love. For Sonakshi Sinha (@aslisona) and Zaheer Iqbal (@iamzahero), togetherness has never been about grand gestures. It’s love distilled to its essentials—a shared home, an easy silence, and the same laughter that started it all.
For Manifest’s July-August cover, the couple lets us in on what “forever” actually looks like, unguarded and unhurried. “I think people really tend to scare you about how your life is going to change after marriage,” says Sonakshi, adding, “but the beauty of it, for us at least, is that things haven’t changed at all. It still feels like I’m his girlfriend and he’s my boyfriend.”
Between banter and blessing, stillness and spontaneity, they’ve found the rare thing most couples spend a lifetime chasing. A forever kind of love.

Porsche is pushing the boundaries of electric performance with the upcoming Cayenne Electric.
Ahead of its official debut, the all-electric luxury SUV was put through an extraordinary high-speed test at California’s Mojave Air and Space Port, where it accelerated alongside the Stratolaunch Roc, the world’s largest aircraft by wingspan. Powered by more than 1,100 horsepower, the prototype exceeded 160 mph (257 km/h) while demonstrating the stability, precision, and performance expected from Porsche’s next-generation electric flagship.
Designed to combine everyday luxury with supercar-level performance, the Cayenne Electric represents Porsche’s most ambitious SUV yet signaling a new era where electrification and high performance go hand in hand.
@stratolaunch_llc @porscheusa
posts.alt_text:
@Balenciaga dropped its Spring Summer 2026 preview collection in Mumbai last night, and the energy in the room felt different.

With Fatima Sana Sheikh, Bobby Deol, Mouni Roy, Sanya Malhotra, Malavika Mohanan, and Krithi Shetty in attendance, it felt less like a formal showcase and more like a real moment around fashion. The room was sharp, observant, and engaged.

Fatima Sana Shaikh said it best: “Balenciaga always has a chic approach and the brand is now heading towards it even more aggressively.” And that tone carried through the evening. Nothing felt loud for attention, yet everything commanded it.

What stood out was how people responded. There was curiosity, closer inspection, and genuine interest in the details. Some silhouettes felt familiar but more refined, while others brought a quiet sense of drama without trying too hard.

That is when a collection works.
Not when it demands attention, but when it earns it. 

@balenciaga #Balenciaga

On Monday night in Manhattan, the cast of Ryan Murphy’s “The Shards" gathered to celebrate the show's premiere. On the show, a prep-school thriller based on Bret Easton Ellis’s 2023 novel about teenage life in 1980s Los Angeles, Homer Gere and Kaia Gerber play wealthy high schoolers who left to their own devices, throwing parties and speeding down Mulholland Drive while a serial killer terrorizes the city.

Despite her rapport with her Gere now, Gerber insists she had never met the young actor, whose father, Richard Gere, was married to her mother, Cindy Crawford, from 1991 to 1995. Still, Murphy was sensitive about the history, as the show is set in the a stylized version of the city where their parents hung out — and met.

Guests attended a screening of the first episode then headed down the street to the Hotel Chelsea for a gathering filled with paraphernalia of the era: wayfarer-style sunglasses, MTV pins, View-Masters and Pat Benatar tapes. 

After watching cast members snort cocaine, pop Klonopin pills and slam vodka sodas onscreen, our reporter @sophiajune said party felt mellow. Tap the link in our bio to get an inside look at the premiere party and see more photos. Photos by @ye.fan

posts.caption:
Among the chic confines of Meadow Lane, Sammy Nussdorf's gourmet grocery store in TriBeCa, the scion and TikTok star found his calling. Normally brimming with influencers, rich moms and finance bros picking up lunch, the store's shelves are carefully arranged with prepared foods, artisanal snacks and an eclectic mix of beverages.
The opening of Meadow Lane was not without drama. A long permit purgatory delayed the store's launch. TikTok-driven lines greeted the store's eventual opening, and the kitchen struggled to keep up with demand. On day three, videos pinged across social media showing their undercooked chicken nuggets, which became international news. At the same time, Nussdorf was criticized for selling such high-priced goods, like the $65 olive oil and the $12 chicken salad.
Yet the store continued to draw crowds, and still does. How did Meadow Lane become such a thriving business in such a short time? Now that chaos of the early days is now behind him, we caught up with Nussdorf about @meadowlanenyc. Tap the link in our bio to read the full story. Photos by @thechrisperez

posts.caption:
The ruched (or puckered or scrunched) loafer looks like a standard lithe loafer until you hit the toe, which wrinkles like a shirt in need of ironing.
Tom Ford’s ruched slip-ons run to $1,190. Saint Laurent offers them in glossy leather and tan suede and even makes one with a collapsible heel. (Two unshakable shoe trends in one!) The Row, the agreed-upon originator of the scrunched toe, introduced its $1,290 Soft Loafer several years ago.
There are versions for men and women, evidence of eroding gender fault lines in the footwear market. All of these ruched-toed shoes seem, at first search, to cost more than $1,000. But what about the wrinkly toe makes the cost worth it to fashion lovers?
@jacobwgallagher analyzes the trend in his latest newsletter. Tap the link in our bio to read more and to subscribe to The Fashions. Photos by Gilbert Carrasquillo/GC Images, Saint Laurent, Tom Ford, Neil Mockford/GC Images

While promoting “The Odyssey” this month, Zendaya wore a pair of earrings made from gold discs from ancient Iran, dating to the first millennium B.C., according to Barron London, a gallery specializing in rare jewels and stones. The actress, with the help of her stylist Law Roach, is known for theme dressing, but the earrings have sparked debate in the world of archaeology and cultural preservation.
Some archaeologists saw the repurposing of ancient artifacts as disrespectful to the cultures they belong and worried about the origins of the pieces. But some believe the mainstreaming of ancient artifacts is a positive reminder of a country's historical legacy.
This was not the first time celebrities have accessorized with historical artifacts. Are they here to stay on the red carpet? Tap the link in our bio to read what archaeologists think of the choice. Photo by Scott A Garfitt/Invision, via @apnews

posts.caption:
In 1995, #Valentino took #ClaudiaSchiffer for a dip in Rome’s Trevi Fountain to recreate #AnitaEkberg’s legendary scene from #LaDolceVita for its Spring 1995 campaign. Built in the 18th century, the Baroque fountain is one of the world’s most recognisable symbols, long associated with dreams, desire and the promise of returning to Rome.
So, when #Fendi funded the $3 million restoration in 2013, it came as no surprise that the house was granted the opportunity to stage its 90th anniversary “Legends and Fairy Tales” Couture collection inside the fountain. Italian brands, from Bvlgari to Dolce & Gabbana, continue to reference the iconic landmark in their designs, a symbol of everything luxury wants to embody: heritage, craftsmanship, fantasy and a beauty that feels eternal.
posts.alt_text: As the tour comes to a close, #LawRoach gives us one last Spider-Man look, this time #Zendaya in London wearing #TamaraRalph Fall 2026 #HauteCouture

posts.caption:
They say it’s what’s inside that counts, and that’s certainly the case for these #Chanel Fall 2026 #HauteCouture jackets. What looked like deceptively simple tweed jackets on the runway tells a completely different story once opened, revealing silk linings covered in illustrations depicting the very fairy tales that inspired #MatthieuBlazy’s collection. Hidden inside are scenes from Jack and the Beanstalk, Goldilocks, and Puss in Boots.
A jacket lining, which traditionally functions to conceal construction and provide comfort, is turned into a private work of art reserved only for the wearer. It’s such a beautiful continuation of the collection’s theme of hidden narratives, where some of the details aren’t immediately visible from the outside.
posts.alt_text: As the tour comes to a close, #LawRoach gives us one last Spider-Man look, this time #Zendaya in London wearing #TamaraRalph Fall 2026 #HauteCouture

posts.caption:
#Chloé may have just released the most beautiful campaign of Fall 2026 so far. Starring #RaquelZimmermann and photographed by legendary duo @inezandvinoodh, it’s a folkloric fantasy that perfectly captures #ChemenaKamali’s romantic vision for the French house.
I remember seeing the collection debut, it was a #KateBush in the ‘70s meets handmade clothes passed down from mother to daughter. Chloé’s bohemian heritage came to life through ruffles, delicate lace, sheer silks, Victorian-inspired blouses, folkloric dresses and sweeping capes, creating a wardrobe that felt both nostalgic and romantic.

posts.caption:
#Gabbriette’s gothic @matieresfecales wedding wardrobe was one of the most beautiful I’ve seen this year and a welcome change from the minimalist gowns that have dominated bridal trends.
The ceremony gown, titled “Gabriella,” was a mutated and distressed Victorian-inspired silk taffeta dress reminiscent of Winona Ryder’s red dress in Bram Stoker’s #Dracula (1992), complete with a four layer bustle.
For the rehearsal dinner, an old Maison Margiela dress of the brides was modified by adding layers of hand-cut, distressed tulle. The third look was a tailored leather suit paired with a satin top hat by #StephenJones. Each look completed with a custom pair of #ChristianLouboutin x #MatièresFécales curved heels.

posts.caption:
The #MiddleEast has produced some of the world’s greatest designers, but why do so many come from #Lebanon? Sat at the crossroads of Silk Road trade routes linking Asia, Europe, and Africa, Lebanon developed a tradition of textiles and embroidery, with skills passed down through generations.
Couture is a huge market In the Middle East due to the social culture of weddings and events. While Haute Couture is an institutional system in Paris,  the concept has existed for centuries across India, Pakistan, the Middle East, and China. In the West, couture works as a prestige marketing tool, elsewhere this level of craftsmanship has always been part of how people dress.
Unlike heritage brands which became corporatised and part of conglomerates, Lebanon’s couture boom produced independent designers like #ZuhairMurad, #ElieSaab, and #GeorgesHobeika, who still lead their own houses. Their success built on craftsmanship, personal reputation, and loyal private clients.

India's Renee Noronha has won first place in the 18-24 category at the Ironman Philippines. Completing the gruelling challenge at 15:55:37, the 20-year-old IIT Madras student upheld held her record of being the youngest Indian female Ironman finisher.
Renee battled torrential rains and unforgiving temperatures to complete the race. In conversation with SheThePeople, the triathlete also revealed that she participated on day 3 of her period, making the victory a profound reminder of her strength and resilience as a woman.
With this win, Renee has now qualified for the Ironman World Championship Hawaii, scheduled for October 2026. She is also on a mission to set a new Guinness world record to become the youngest person in the world to do a full Ironman on 6 continents. She is on track to achieve this by April 2027, at the age of 21.
Read full interview at www.shethepeople.tv. | @renee.noronha

India's Renee Noronha has won first place in the 18-24 category at the Ironman Philippines. Completing the gruelling challenge at 15:55:37, the 20-year-old IIT Madras student upheld held her record of being the youngest Indian female Ironman finisher.

Renee battled torrential rains and unforgiving temperatures to complete the race. In conversation with SheThePeople, the triathlete also revealed that she participated on day 3 of her period, making the victory a profound reminder of her strength and resilience as a woman.

With this win, Renee has now qualified for the Ironman World Championship Hawaii, scheduled for October 2026. She is also on a mission to set a new Guinness world record to become the youngest person in the world to do a full Ironman on 6 continents. She is on track to achieve this by April 2027, at the age of 21.

Read full interview at www.shethepeople.tv. | @renee.noronha

posts.caption:
What happens when an artist’s heart flutters like a butterfly between two skills? To gain the response to this question, we have to observe Prachi Saathi’s life closely.
When she was a child, her mother enrolled her at the Prithvi summer camp, where she began to learn voice-dubbing, a skill she picked up without purpose. Later, she got an opportunity to work as a voice-dubbing actor in a children’s film, Karamati Coat, which gained her recognition in the field.
Today, she is a renowned voice-dubbing actress. Prachi, who has been the official Hindi dubbing voice for Disney character Minnie Mouse, has voice-dubbed over 200 character roles in foreign animation media in the Indian dubbing industry. She is also a Bharatanatyam dancer and is currently training under her Guru, Smt. Rama Vaidyanathan.

posts.caption:
As Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey makes headlines worldwide, along with Matt Damon's ripped look, the Oscar winner shares an unexpected behind-the-scenes revelation about the film. He captured everyone’s attention when he mentioned that behind some of the film's memorable arm shots, his stunt double was a woman, Devyn Dalton.
Damon extended his appreciation, saying he was impressed by her biceps and incredible strength. “When we did the forced perspective stuff of the Laestrygonians - I don’t know if there’s been a thing about how we did it- there were these stunt men who were all seven feet,” the actor shared, reflecting on The Odyssey. “And then they got stuntmen who were under five feet, and so my double was a woman, a female stunt performer, who had the greatest arms I’ve ever seen,” he added.
